q: How does a university calculate its campus carbon footprint?
title: University campus carbon footprint
short: Start with what the campus pays for: electricity, diesel for gensets and buses, LPG in hostels and canteens, and refrigerant top-ups. That is Scope 1 and 2. Then add staff and student travel, purchases and waste in Scope 3, which is usually larger.

ul: Diesel for gensets and campus buses.
LPG for hostel kitchens and labs.
Refrigerant refills for ACs and cold rooms.

p: Commuting, flights for conferences, books and equipment, construction and waste. Survey commuting once a year.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
